_about: The discovery net: how a tool gets onto our radar, so a good one is never left out because nobody happened to look. Discovery and scoring are separate: these signals put a tool in the check queue; only public data (users, market, critics and value) ever moves a score. Rules are enforced by coverageReport() in index.ts and shown on /desk.
rules: One trigger is enough. If a tool trips any trigger below, it enters the check queue.

Every tool in the queue is checked within one monthly cycle: count its citable reviews on foundation sources, read the lists that name it, and record its category. An unchecked entry past its due month shows as overdue on /desk.
Every check ends in one of three outcomes, written down: scored, in the wings (with the real counts and what's missing), or dropped (with the reason, kept in the log).
If a tool's category has no scoreboard yet, it goes to Stephanie the same month with every tool stuck in it, so the decision to build a board is made on purpose.
Discovery never moves a score. A nomination, a follower spike or a vendor submission gets a tool checked; it never gets a tool ranked higher.

Never put a verified professional reputation tool on a scored board, and keep reference checking and candidate verification tools off the ranked lists: hiring.productions shares RepVera's owner (16 CFR 465.6; GROWTH.md). RepVera is listed in its own category with no score and no rank, always with Stephanie's note that she built it.

triggers.label: Named on a current, independent best-of list
triggers.note: One list puts it in the queue. Two make it a contender.

triggers.label: Top 10 by review count in its G2 category, or by users in its Chrome Web Store category
triggers.note: Checked for every category we cover and every category in research.

triggers.label: Review count up 50% or more in a year
triggers.note: Measured from Internet Archive snapshots, the same way we caught Manatal's rise.

triggers.label: Stephanie nominates it
triggers.note: Her 20 years in hiring help find tools worth checking. A nomination gets a tool checked and has no effect on its score.

triggers.label: Recruiters recommend it in the communities we read
triggers.note: Recruiting Brainfood, RecruitingDaily, SourceCon and r/recruiting. Discovery only: none of these feed a score.

triggers.label: People search for it
triggers.note: If people are searching "is X worth it" or "X vs Y", we owe them a check.

triggers.label: Employers ask for it by name in job postings
triggers.note: Hiring tools only. "Experience with X" in a posting means real teams run it.

triggers.label: Listed in the integration marketplace of an ATS we rank
triggers.note: Teams don't integrate tools they don't use.

triggers.label: Readers ask for it
triggers.note: Anyone can nominate a tool. Every request is logged.

triggers.label: The vendor submits it
triggers.note: Listing is free. Submitting gets a tool checked, never scored higher.

triggers.label: Added by the editors
triggers.note: Used only for entries from before Nov 2026, when the trigger wasn't recorded.

notSignals.label: LinkedIn and social follower counts
notSignals.why: They measure marketing reach and tell you nothing about whether the product works. Followers can be bought, they swell with job posts and founders' personal brands, and LinkedIn's terms bar collecting them at scale. A sudden jump can prompt a check. It never moves a score.

notSignals.label: Awards and badges
notSignals.why: Many are tied to entry fees or sponsorship. They count only when the judging is independent and published.

notSignals.label: A vendor's own best-tools list
notSignals.why: It ranks itself first. We show those lists and never count them.
